options: Positive peaks of input clipped at +12V and negative peaks at –6V
Positive peaks of input clipped at +6V and negative peaks at –12 V
Positive peaks of input clipped at +12V and negative peaks at –12 V
Positive peaks of input clipped at +6V and negative peaks at –6 V
questions.explanation:
Solution: During the positive half-cycle of input (Vi > 0) diode D1 branch : diode D1 will be forward-biased and conduct only when the voltage at its cathode. The cathode is connected to a +12 V source.
So, D1 conducts when Vo > 12V. When D1 conducts, it acts like a short circuit, clamping the output voltage Vo to +12V.
For any input voltage that would cause Vo to exceed +12V, the output will be limited to +12V.
Diode D2 branch: Diode D2 will be forward-biased only when the voltage at its anode (6V) is greater than the voltage at its cathode (Vo).
So, D2 conducts when –6V > Vo. During the positive half-cycle, Vo is always positive. The condition –6V > Vo can never be met.
Therefore, D2 remains reverse-biased (an open circuit) through out the entire positive half-cycle.
Conclusion for positive cycle: The output voltage follows the input until it reaches +12V, at which point it gets clipped.
During the negative half-cycle of input (Vi < 0)
* diode D1 branch : The condition for D1 conduct is Vo > 12 V.
* During the negative half-cycle, Vo is negative, so this condition is never met.
* Therefore, D1 remains reverse-biased (an open circuit) throughout the entire negative half-cycle.
* Diode D2 branch: Diode D2 will be forward-biased when the voltage at its anode (–6V) is greater than the voltage at its cathode (Vo).
* So, D2 conducts when –6V > Vo.
* This means that whenever the output voltage tries to become more negative than –6V, diode D2 will turn on.
* When D2 conducts, it acts like a short circuit, clamping the output voltage Vo to –6V.
Conclusion for negative cycle : The output voltage follows the input until it reaches –6V, at which point it gets clipped.
The circuit clips the sinusoidal waveform as follows:
The positive peak is clipped at +12V.
The negative peak is clipped at –6V.
Therefore, the correct answer is option 1
